title: Pin-ended column: elastic buckling factor

source.work: Bentley Systems, STAAD.Pro Help, Verification Examples (public documentation, docs.bentley.com)
source.edition: STAAD.Pro Help v21 build (pages refer to the STAAD.Pro 2023 sample files), read 2026-11-22
source.notes: problem statement taken from the vendor page (text and input listing). The page cites: no textbook; the page validates with Pcr = pi^2 E I / L^2 - NOT opened for this project; no number is taken from it. The page's 'theory' values are recorded as printed; the program's own results are not used.

analysis: Plane problem in the global X-Y plane (Y vertical); the out-of-plane DOFs (uz, rx, ry) of every node are held; in-plane bending about local z. Column of 30 ft = 360 in, pinned at both ends (the top free to move axially), W10x45 with the moment of inertia the page uses, I = 248 in^4, E = 29,730 ksi; axial load 160 kip. Linear buckling analysis; target: the buckling factor Pcr / 160. The engine's member carries the exact stability functions. The area does not enter (placeholder 10 in^2); Iy = 1000 Iz so that the in-plane mode is the lowest. Reference values: computed here from this statement (verification/derive/vendor_reference.py); the textbook cited by the vendor page was not opened and no number is taken from it.

targets.precisionNote: evaluated here in double precision (smallest root of the characteristic equation sin(kL) = 0, P = k^2 EI); tolerance = policy floor 1e-6
printed "3.509"; tolerance = half a unit in the last printed digit
